associations.rationale: The conjunction states finiteness of positive roots, that every finite free indecomposable has a positive-root dimension vector, and existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism for every positive root, directly formalizing Gabriel's classification theorem.

This proves only that the set of positive roots of a Dynkin diagram is finite; it supports the theorem's finiteness conclusion once the classification is available but does not itself state finiteness of indecomposable representations.

This is a root-recognition lemma for nonnegative nonzero vectors of Cartan norm two, rather than a statement about dimension vectors of indecomposable quiver representations, so it supplies supporting root-theoretic evidence.

For every positive root, the formal type directly gives an indecomposable representation with that dimension vector and proves uniqueness up to isomorphism, exactly the existence-and-uniqueness clause of Gabriel's theorem.
